The 5 seconds it takes for the space shuttle to pass a point is significant because it provides the time duration during which the entire length of the shuttle can be observed as it moves past that point. This information allows us to calculate the length of the shuttle using its speed, which we determine from the height and time given in the problem.

Here’s how:

1. **Calculate Speed**: First, use the height (700 meters) and time (40 seconds) to find the speed of the space shuttle.
   \[
   \text{Speed} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}} = \frac{700 \text{ m}}{40 \text{ s}} = 17.5 \text{ m/s}
   \]

2. **Determine Length**: Next, use the speed (17.5 m/s) and the time it takes to pass a point (5 seconds) to find the length of the space shuttle.
   \[
   \text{Length} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time} = 17.5 \text{ m/s} \times 5 \text{ s} = 87.5 \text{ m}
   \]
